newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Premier says won't raise Discovery bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Premier says won't raise Discovery bid.

text.p: Premier Oil Plc said on Thursday it was unlikely to again raise its offer price for Discovery Petroleum Nl.
"This is the bid at the moment that we can justify, based upon our recent evaluation," Premier international manager Steve Lowden told reporters.
"I can't see us getting access to any more data," Lowden said.
Premier earlier on Thursday raised its bid for Discovery to 80 cents a share from 70 cents, increasing the value of its offer to A$106.5 million from A$91.9 million.
The bid was increased after Lowden met with Discovery executives in Perth earlier this week and discussed the Australian company's production and exploration portfolio.
Lowden, who returns to London on Friday, said he planned to discuss the offer with Discovery executives in the near future.

He said Discovery was a good fit for Premier's strategy in the Asia/Pacific region and he did not expect that the bid would fail, even though speculators had constantly pushed the share price above that offered by Premier.
Discovery shares were four cents higher at 81 cents at 3.15 p.m. (0415 gmt) on Thursday.
Lowden said he had received a reasonably positive response from Discovery shareholders when the bid was pitched at 70 cents per share.
This price compared with 52 cents for Discovery stock just before Premier launched its bid.
Premier is seeking a minimum of 50.1 percent control, with the bid set to close one month later on December 11.

While a report prepared by Grant Samuel and Associates and commissioned by Discovery valued the shares at between 77 and 95 cents, Lowden said the upper end of the range contained a lot of blue sky, especially with the Australian exploration acreage.
"We are certainly in no position to see any further value in the company. We consider there to be a fair amount of blue sky in the upper end of the Grant Samuel report," Lowden said.
Papua New Guinea-based producer and explorer Oil Search Ltd purchased a 10.1 percent stake in Discovery after the initial Premier bid, paying 75 cents per share.
Lowden said he had not discussed the bid with Oil Search but had met the company recently to discuss regional operations.
He said Premier would be a better fit with Discovery than Oil Search and could not rule out a rival bid.
